title: Vite, kjenne eller kunne — three kinds of knowing
goal: Choose vite for facts, kjenne for familiarity, and kunne for a learned skill or ability.

objectives.statement: Choose vite for facts, kjenne for familiarity, and kunne for a learned skill or ability.

sections.title: A first shift at the community centre

spans.value: Lea has recently moved to Trondheim. On Saturday she is helping at a neighbourhood event for the first time. Arne, one of the organisers, shows her around.

blocks.translation: Do you know where the kitchen is?

spans.value: Ja, det er i gangen til venstre. Men jeg kjenner ikke bygningen så godt ennå.

blocks.translation: Yes, it’s in the corridor on the left. But I don’t know the building very well yet.

spans.value: Kjenner du Mari? Hun har ansvaret for maten.

blocks.translation: Do you know Mari? She is in charge of the food.

spans.value: Nei, men jeg vet hvem hun er. Vi har ikke snakket sammen før.

blocks.translation: No, but I know who she is. We haven’t spoken before.

spans.value: Kan du lage kaffe med den store maskinen?

blocks.translation: Do you know how to make coffee with the large machine?

spans.value: Ja, jeg kan bruke en slik maskin. Jeg jobbet på kafé før.

blocks.translation: Yes, I know how to use that kind of machine. I used to work in a café.

spans.value: Flott. Vet du når gjestene kommer?

blocks.translation: Great. Do you know when the guests are coming?

spans.value: De kommer klokka to, tror jeg.

blocks.translation: They’re coming at two, I think.

items.value: is used for facts and information.
is used for familiarity with a person, place, or thing.
is used for a learned skill or ability.

en.value: to know a fact → know/knows
to be familiar with → know/knows
to know how to do something → can/know how to

when knowledge can be understood as information: a time, an address, a reason, an answer, or some other fact.

en.value: Do you know where the kitchen is?

spans.value: The location of the kitchen is information. Lea can give that information as an answer.

en.value: I know where the kitchen is.

en.value: She knows why the bus is delayed.

sections.title: Kjenne: being familiar with someone or something

spans.value: when the point is familiarity gained through contact or experience. You may
a person because you have met and interacted with them. You may also
a city, neighbourhood, building, book, or type of situation because it is familiar to you.

en.value: Do you know Mari?

spans.value: He is not asking whether Lea has information about Mari. He wants to know whether Mari is personally familiar to her.

no.value: Nei, men jeg vet hvem hun er.

en.value: No, but I know who she is.
I know Mari.
I know who Mari is.

spans.value: The first sentence suggests personal familiarity. The second says only that the speaker knows Mari’s identity. You can know who someone is without knowing that person personally.
The same distinction appears with places.

en.value: I know Trondheim quite well.
I know where Trondheim is.

spans.value: In the first sentence, the speaker is familiar with the city. Perhaps they have lived there, visited often, or know their way around. In the second, the speaker knows a geographical fact.

en.value: Do you know the new neighbour?

no.value: Jeg kjenner ikke dette området så godt.

en.value: I don’t know this area very well.
She is already familiar with the restaurant.
We know her family well.

no.value: Han kjenner systemet etter mange år i firmaet.

en.value: He knows the system after many years at the company.

spans.value: often means to be familiar with something or to know of its existence.

en.value: Are you familiar with this author?

no.value: Jeg kjenner til problemet, men jeg vet ikke alle detaljene.

en.value: I am aware of the problem, but I don’t know all the details.

spans.value: Return to Lea’s first day at the community centre. Imagine she has seen Mari’s name on the schedule but has never spoken to her. Describe what Lea knows using one sentence about Mari’s identity and one sentence about personal familiarity.

sections.title: Kunne: having a learned skill or ability

spans.value: when someone has learned how to do something or has the ability to do it. Its present form is
At the community centre, Arne asks:

no.value: Kan du lage kaffe med den store maskinen?

en.value: Do you know how to make coffee with the large machine?

spans.value: Lea has used this type of machine before, so she answers:

no.value: Jeg kan bruke en slik maskin.

en.value: I know how to use that kind of machine.

spans.value: is normally followed by the infinitive without

en.value: I can swim.
She knows how to repair bicycles.
Do you know how to use this program?
He cannot drive.

spans.value: A language can also be treated as a learned ability.

en.value: Do you know Norwegian?
She knows a little Spanish.

spans.value: Keep the focus on an ability the person possesses. Compare factual knowledge with practical ability:

en.value: I know how the coffee machine works.
I know how to use the coffee machine.

spans.value: The first sentence concerns information about the machine’s operation. The second says that the speaker has the practical ability to operate it. Someone might understand how a machine works in theory but still be unable to use it confidently.

no.value: Emil vet hvordan man skifter et dekk.

en.value: Emil knows how to change a tyre.
Emil knows how to change a tyre.

spans.value: reports knowledge of the procedure. The sentence with
presents changing a tyre as Emil’s skill.

Use the event context again. Lea has read and understood the operating procedure for the sound system, but she has never operated it. Describe her factual knowledge of how the system works, then state whether the available context supports saying that she has the practical skill to use it.
The difference becomes clearer when all three verbs appear in similar questions.

en.value: Do you know who the pianist is?

spans.value: This asks for a fact: the pianist’s identity.

en.value: Do you know the pianist?
Can you play the piano?

spans.value: This asks about a learned skill.

en.value: Do you know where the swimming pool is?
Are you familiar with the swimming pool?
Can you swim?

spans.value: The first question asks for location information. The second asks whether the place is familiar. The third asks about an ability.

no.value: Vet du hva dette programmet heter?

en.value: Do you know what this program is called?
Are you familiar with this program?
Do you know how to use this program?

spans.value: These questions could all arise in one conversation, but they request different kinds of knowledge.

For each of several shared topics—a colleague, a town, a computer program, and a musical instrument—form or complete questions that ask separately about a fact, familiarity, and a learned ability. Keep each topic constant while changing the kind of knowing. ## Common mistakes {#common-mistakes role=contrast objectives=obj-knowing-verbs-vite-kjenne-kunne-01}

spans.value: For an ordinary neutral statement that someone has learned and can perform an action, normally use
, such as the following, can occur in marked or idiomatic contexts, but they are not the usual neutral choices for the meanings intended here.

en.value: I know how to swim.

She knows how to play guitar.

spans.value: Assuming familiarity always includes detailed facts
Being familiar with something does not mean knowing every fact about it.

no.value: Jeg kjenner byen, men jeg vet ikke hvor det nye biblioteket er.

en.value: I know the city, but I don’t know where the new library is.

spans.value: Likewise, factual knowledge does not necessarily mean personal familiarity.

no.value: Jeg vet mye om forfatteren, men jeg kjenner henne ikke.

en.value: I know a lot about the author, but I don’t know her personally.

spans.value: Later that morning, after Mari, Lea, and Arne have spent time setting up rooms and talking together, Mari and Lea go into the kitchen to prepare coffee.
Hei, Lea. Nå har vi jobbet sammen en stund. Kjenner du Arne fra før?

blocks.translation: Hi, Lea. We’ve been working together for a while now. Did you know Arne before today?

spans.value: Nei, jeg møtte ham i dag. Men etter at vi har jobbet sammen, kjenner jeg både deg og Arne litt nå.

blocks.translation: No, I met him today. But after working together, I know both you and Arne a little now.

spans.value: Vet du hvor vi skal sette koppene?

blocks.translation: Do you know where we should put the cups?
Yes, Arne showed me the cupboard.

spans.value: Bra. Kan du også lage te med denne maskinen?

blocks.translation: Good. Do you also know how to make tea with this machine?

spans.value: Det kan jeg. Nå kjenner jeg kjøkkenet ganske godt også.

blocks.translation: I can do that. Now I know the kitchen quite well too.

prompt.value: Fullfør hver setning med verbet som passer til betydningen.

explanation.value: «Vet» viser at noen har en opplysning om sted, tid, årsak eller et annet faktum.

spans.value: at møtet begynner klokka ni. Lea

prompt.value: Arne har pekt ut Mari for Lea på et personalbilde, men Lea og Mari har aldri snakket sammen. Skriv to separate norske setninger til en kollega: si hva Lea vet om Mari, og om de kjenner hverandre personlig.

payload.judge_prompt: Vurder om første setning uttrykker en sann opplysning om hvem Mari er eller hvilken rolle hun har, om den andre uttrykker manglende personlig kjennskap, og om svaret består av to separate setninger. Godta naturlige bokmålsformuleringer uten å kreve bestemte ordvalg.

criteria.instruction: States a true identity fact about Mari that Lea knows from the context, such as Mari's role or workplace; accept natural phrasing without requiring the exact words «vet hvem».
Makes clear that Lea and Mari are not personally acquainted; accept natural phrasing such as «Lea kjenner ikke Mari» or «de har aldri møttes».
Uttrykker identitetsfaktaet og den personlige kjennskapen i nøyaktig to setninger.
Distinguishes factual knowledge of Mari's identity from personal acquaintance, using a natural valid Norwegian expression for each.

prompt.value: Lea har lært hvordan lydanlegget fungerer, men har aldri brukt det. Skriv to setninger på norsk til Arne: Fortell hva Lea vet, og om vi vet at hun kan bruke anlegget. Bruk «vet hvordan» og «kan».

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate procedure-knowledge, ability-status and two-sentence form. Accept natural Bokmål variants, but require both target meanings, the forms vet hvordan and kan, and exactly two sentences.

criteria.instruction: States that Lea knows how the sound system works, using vet hvordan.
States that the available facts do not establish whether Lea can operate it, using kan.
Uses exactly two Norwegian sentences.
Requires factual procedure knowledge to be expressed with vet hvordan and practical ability with kan.

prompt.value: Skriv en melding på norsk fra Lea til Ingrid om den første arbeidsdagen. Fortell hvor koppene skal stå, hvem Lea snakket og jobbet med, at Mari står på arbeidsplanen, og hva Lea kan gjøre med temaskinen. Bruk «vite», «kjenne» og «kunne» der de passer.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate cup-information, organiser-familiarity, schedule-information, tea-ability, message-purpose and verb-choice as binding. The visible task asks for the three target verbs.

criteria.instruction: Communicates that Lea knows where the cups belong.
Communicates that Lea is now somewhat familiar with Mari and Arne.
Communicates the fact that Mari is on the work schedule.
Communicates that Lea can make tea with the machine.
Produces a coherent message to Ingrid about Lea's day.
Uses vite for facts, kjenne for familiarity and kunne for practical ability. This distinction is required.

text.value: «Arne viste meg hvor koppene skal stå, og jeg jobbet og snakket med Mari og Arne.»

prompt.value: Fullfør setningene med verbet som passer til situasjonen.

explanation.value: En opplysning fra personallista er kunnskap. Kontakt skaper kjennskap, og tidligere bruk av programmet viser en praktisk ferdighet.

prompt.value: Skriv et svar på norsk til reisefølget. Fortell hvem som vet hvor hotellet ligger, hvem som kjenner Bergen, og hvem som kan kjøre. Bruk «vite», «kjenne» og «kunne».

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate hotel-fact, bergen-familiarity, driving-ability, correct use of vite, kjenne and kunne, and group-reply. Require the reply to use vite for the hotel fact, kjenne for familiarity with Bergen, and kunne for driving ability, while accurately distinguishing the three meanings.

criteria.instruction: States that Eva knows the hotel's address or location using vite.
States that Eva is familiar with Bergen using kjenne and does not attribute that familiarity to Jon.
States that Jon can drive in heavy city traffic using kunne and does not attribute that ability to Eva.
Produces a coherent reply for the travel group.
Requires that the location fact uses vite, city familiarity uses kjenne and driving ability uses kunne.

«Jeg vet ikke hvor hotellet ligger. Jeg har aldri vært i Bergen, men jeg har kjørt trygt i tett bytrafikk i ti år.»

prompt.value: Skriv en dialog på norsk mellom Per og Liv. Per spør når konserten begynner, om Liv kjenner Ada personlig, og om hun kan bruke lydutstyret. Liv svarer på alle tre spørsmålene. Konserten begynner klokka 19.30. Liv og Ada har jobbet sammen før, og Liv har brukt utstyret på tre konserter.

payload.judge_prompt: Evaluate time-exchange, singer-exchange, equipment-exchange and exchange-form. Require the target verbs for factual knowledge, personal acquaintance and practical ability.

criteria.instruction: Includes Per's question about the starting time and Liv's answer that it is 19.30.
Includes a question about personal acquaintance with Ada and an affirmative answer supported by their earlier work together.
Includes a question about operating the sound equipment and an affirmative answer supported by Liv's prior experience.
Produces a coherent exchange between Per and Liv.
Uses vite for the time question, kjenne for acquaintance and kunne for equipment ability.
